docs.title: Verification status
docs.text:
"Verified" has a narrow, checkable meaning in Nephilex 0.11.0:

  1. The rewritten line no longer matches the rule (or matches the rule's recognized safe form). This check runs both for --patches and for nephilex fix.
  2. nephilex fix also re-parses the whole changed file for Python, JSON and YAML files, and drops all fixes for a file that would no longer parse.

By default it does not run your tests, start the application, or prove that the new code behaves the same. nephilex fix --verify-with-tests adds that check: it runs your test command before and after the fixes in a temporary copy of the repository and commits only fixes that keep the tests passing (see Fixing & pull requests). Either way, review the change as you would any other pull request.

The re-scan of the fixed branch (nephilex scan . --no-ai -q), trimmed to the summary and the rows for app.py:45. The first line is the folder name, which was fixrepo in this run:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────── Nephilex scan ──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ fixrepo                                                                                                   │
│ Aggregate risk: 99.7/100   Findings: 19                                                                   │
│ Critical: 2 | High: 7 | Medium: 9 | Low: 1 | Info: 0                                                      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│ Medium   │ 44.3 │ Cross-site scripting (tainted     │ app.py:45        │ ast-python.ast-xss               │
│          │      │ value returned as HTML)           │                  │                                  │

The yaml.load finding is gone, and so is the other fixed finding (21 before, 19 after). The cross-site scripting finding on the same line is still there: safe_load stops object construction, but the view still returns request data as HTML. One fixed finding does not make the line safe.

Why the weak hash on line 50 is not fixed

hash_password hashes a password with MD5. Swapping in SHA-256 would make the rule stop matching, but SHA-256 is also a fast hash, so stored passwords would stay easy to crack. Password storage needs a slow key-derivation function (bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2), which a one-line rewrite cannot introduce. Nephilex therefore offers no automatic fix for a line that hashes a password or secret, and the finding stays with that guidance. Treat verified fixes as a correct first step, not the last one.

docs.title: Reproduce it
docs.text:
pipx install "nephilex[ast]"
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/nephilex/nephilex.git
nephilex scan nephilex/examples/vulnerable-app --no-ai --patches -f json -f markdown -o ex

# nephilex fix needs a git repository of its own:
cp -r nephilex/examples/vulnerable-app demo && cd demo
git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "demo app"
nephilex fix --dry-run
nephilex fix -q
nephilex scan . --no-ai -q

Commit hashes, timestamps, the base branch name (master here, from git's default) and the audit-log actor will differ on your machine, and the dependency findings follow live OSV data. These steps were re-run in a fresh folder for this page and gave the same 21 and 18 finding counts.

docs.title: Fixing findings and opening pull requests
docs.text:
nephilex fix turns Nephilex from an advisor into a fixer. It scans a repository, applies the fixes it can verify locally to a new branch, commits them, and, on request, pushes the branch and opens a pull request.

nephilex fix ./my-app --dry-run      # preview only; writes nothing
nephilex fix ./my-app                # apply fixes to a branch and commit locally
nephilex fix ./my-app --open-pr      # also push and open a pull request

docs.title: What gets fixed
docs.text:
Only deterministic, self-verified rewrites are applied by default. These are fixes where Nephilex can transform the exact offending line and then re-check that the detection no longer fires. Current rewrites:

Rule Change patterns.python-yaml-load yaml.load(...) to yaml.safe_load(...) patterns.weak-hash-md5-sha1 MD5 / SHA-1 to SHA-256 patterns.python-shell-true remove shell=True from subprocess calls patterns.tls-verify-disabled re-enable certificate verification patterns.flask-debug-true debug=True to debug=False

Findings without a deterministic rewrite are left for you to fix manually (the scan report still explains them and, with an AI provider, can suggest a patch).

Each applied change preserves the original line's indentation and surrounding code, because the rewrite runs against the real file line rather than a stored snippet.

docs.title: Safety model
docs.text:
• Nothing is written in --dry-run. You see the exact table of changes first.
  • Changes land on a new branch (nephilex/security-fixes by default), never on your working branch, so they are trivial to discard.
  • Nothing is pushed or opened unless you pass --open-pr.
  • Only verified fixes are applied unless you explicitly pass --include-unverified (review those carefully).
  • Tests are opt-in. Nephilex does not run the project's tests unless you pass --verify-with-tests (see below). Your git commit hooks still run when the fixes are committed, unless you pass --no-verify.

docs.title: Verifying fixes with your tests
docs.text:
"Verified" above means the detection rule no longer matches the rewritten line. It does not mean the application still works: switching MD5 to SHA-256 changes stored digests, and removing shell=True breaks a command passed as a string. --verify-with-tests adds a second check by running the project's own test command:

nephilex fix . --verify-with-tests --test-command "python -m pytest -q"
nephilex fix . --test-command "npm test" --test-timeout 900   # --test-command implies it

The command can also come from the project's .nephilex.yml:

autofix:
  test_command: ["python", "-m", "pytest", "-q"]   # or a string: "python -m pytest -q"
  test_timeout: 900                                # seconds per run (default 600)

The config keys are read only when the project config is trusted (local targets; see Which configuration is trusted). A cloned repository can never choose a command Nephilex runs. --test-command and --test-timeout override the config. Without a command, --verify-with-tests stops with a usage error (exit code 2). It cannot be combined with --dry-run.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. Nephilex creates a temporary git worktree from the scanned commit (HEAD). Your working tree is never used to run anything, and the worktree is removed at the end, also after an error or a timeout.
  2. The test command runs once in that worktree before any fix (the baseline). If it fails or times out, the fixes cannot be judged: Nephilex reports that, marks every fix "could not verify", commits nothing and exits 1.
  3. The fixes are applied in the worktree and the project is scanned again. A fix fails if its finding is still reported, or if a new High or Critical finding appears in a file it changed. Failed fixes are dropped.
  4. The test command runs again with the remaining fixes applied.
  5. Only fixes whose tests passed are applied to the fix branch, committed, and (with --open-pr) pushed. Nephilex checks that the files it commits are byte for byte the ones the tests ran against (line endings aside).

Each fix gets a test result next to its rule check: passed, failed or could not verify (for example, the run after the fixes timed out). The summary table shows both, with the reason for every fix that was left out. The commit message, the pull request body (a Tests column and a "Test verification" section) and the fix.applied records in the audit log carry the result too.

All fixes are tested together in one run. When that run fails, every fix in it is marked failed and the output says the failing fix was not isolated. Re-run with --scanners or --min-severity, or fix the findings one rule at a time, to narrow it down.

The worktree holds only committed files. Dependencies must already be available (an activated virtual environment, packages on PATH) or be installed by the test command itself. Untracked files such as node_modules/, .env or local build output are not copied, and submodules are not initialized.

docs.title: How the command runs
docs.text:
• No shell. The command is split into a program and arguments (shlex.split on POSIX, the Windows command-line rules on Windows) and run directly. Pipes, && and variable expansion do not work; put them in a script and run the script. A list in autofix.test_command is used as is.
  • Program lookup. A bare name such as pytest is searched only in the absolute directories on PATH, never in the current or the repository directory. A path such as ./scripts/test.sh is resolved inside the worktree.
  • Timeout. Each run is stopped after --test-timeout seconds (default 600), together with the processes it started.
  • Capped output. The last 1 MB of combined output is kept; the last lines are shown when a run fails. Test output is shown only in your terminal. It is never sent to an AI provider and never put in the pull request.
  • Scrubbed environment. Variables that look like credentials are removed before the tests start: names containing TOKEN, SECRET, KEY, PASSWORD, CREDENTIAL, AUTH and similar; whole families such as GITHUB_*, GITLAB_*, AWS_*, AZURE_*, GOOGLE_*, NEPHILEX_*, ANTHROPIC_* and OPENAI_*; SSH_AUTH_SOCK, KUBECONFIG and git variables that redirect git; and any value that holds a password in a URL, a private key or a well-known token format. PATH, HOME, SYSTEMROOT, the temp directories and the variables Python and Node read (VIRTUAL_ENV, PYTHONPATH, NODE_OPTIONS, ...) are kept. The names removed are listed in the summary; their values never are.

docs.title: Remaining risk
docs.text:
Running a project's tests runs that project's code. Only use --verify-with-tests on repositories you trust as much as you would trust running their tests yourself. The controls above stop an accident, such as a test suite reading a token from the environment or writing to your checkout; they are not a sandbox:

  • The tests run as your user, with your file system and network. They can read ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.netrc, browser profiles, and anything else your account can read, and they can reach the network.
  • The environment scrub is a deny list. A secret in an innocently named variable, in an unrecognised format, gets through.
  • On Windows, a process the tests start in the background can outlive a run that finished normally; the process tree is only killed on a timeout.

For an untrusted repository, run nephilex fix without --verify-with-tests and run its tests yourself in a disposable container or VM.

docs.title: Opening a pull request
docs.text:
--open-pr pushes the branch with your normal git credentials, then opens a PR through the host's API with a token from the environment:

Host Token GitHub GITHUB_TOKEN GitLab GITLAB_TOKEN Bitbucket BITBUCKET_TOKEN 
export GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_...
nephilex fix . --open-pr --base main

docs.title: Give the token as little as possible
docs.text:
The token is only used to create the pull request (the push uses your git remote's own credentials), so it does not need broad access:

Host Token to create Permissions GitHub Fine-grained personal access token, limited to the one repository Pull requests: Read and write (Metadata: Read is added automatically). Add Contents: Read and write only if this same token is also what your git remote pushes with GitHub Actions The workflow's built-in GITHUB_TOKEN permissions: { contents: write, pull-requests: write } on that one job, nothing at workflow level GitLab Project access token, role Developer Scope api (creating a merge request needs it); write_repository only if it also pushes Bitbucket Repository access token Pull requests: Write; Repositories: Write only if it also pushes

Avoid a classic GitHub token with the repo scope: it can read and write every repository you can. Set an expiry on whichever token you create, keep it in your secret store rather than a shell profile, and never put it in .nephilex.yml. Nephilex reads the token only to call the host's API, never prints it, and removes it from the environment of --verify-with-tests runs.

The PR description lists every change with its file, line, rule, and whether it was verified, plus the diffs in a collapsible section.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
nephilex fix [TARGET]
      --dry-run              preview changes without writing
      --open-pr              push the branch and open a pull request
      --branch NAME          branch to create (default: nephilex/security-fixes)
      --base NAME            base branch for the PR (default: repo's default branch)
      --include-unverified   also apply fixes that did not self-verify
      --force-branch         reuse/overwrite the branch if it already exists
      --verify-with-tests    run the project's tests before and after the fixes
                             in a temporary worktree; commit only passing fixes
      --test-command CMD     test command (implies --verify-with-tests)
      --test-timeout SECONDS time limit per test run (default 600)
  -s, --scanners a,b         only run these scanners
      --min-severity SEV     only consider findings at/above this severity
  -q, --quiet                suppress progress output

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Completed (fixes applied/committed, or nothing to fix). 1 The workflow stopped with an error (e.g. not a git repo, push failed, no token, or the baseline test run failed with --verify-with-tests). 2 The target could not be resolved, or the options are invalid (e.g. --verify-with-tests without a test command).

With --verify-with-tests, fixes that fail their tests are a normal outcome, not an error: they are left out, the rest are committed, and the exit code is 0.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text: You can wire nephilex fix --open-pr into a scheduled job so Nephilex proposes fix PRs automatically. Give the job a token with permission to push branches and open pull requests, and pin --base to your default branch.

docs.title: Importing SARIF from other scanners
docs.text:
Most teams already run scanners they trust: Semgrep, CodeQL, gitleaks, Trivy, Bandit. Nearly all of them write SARIF 2.1.0. nephilex import reads that output and turns every result into an ordinary Nephilex finding, so the rest of Nephilex works on it unchanged: baselines, the allowlist and exceptions, policy, the severity gate, every report format, enrichment and patch generation.

You keep your scanners. Nephilex adds triage, gating and reporting on top.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# Import one or more SARIF files for the project in the current directory
nephilex import semgrep.sarif codeql.sarif

# Gate CI on the imported results
nephilex import semgrep.sarif --fail-on high

# Write any report format
nephilex import trivy.sarif -f html -o report.html
nephilex import *.sarif -f json -f sarif -o reports/

# Merge imported results into a full Nephilex scan
nephilex scan . --import-sarif semgrep.sarif --import-sarif gitleaks.sarif

nephilex import takes the same reporting and gating options as nephilex scan: -f/--format, -o/--output, --baseline, --diff, --fail-on, --min-severity, --config, --no-ai, --patches, --audience and -q. --project PATH (default: the current directory) is the project root the SARIF paths are relative to.

docs.title: Producing SARIF, per tool
docs.text: Run each tool from the project root so the paths it writes are relative to it.

docs.title: Semgrep
docs.text:
semgrep scan --config auto --sarif --output semgrep.sarif
nephilex import semgrep.sarif

Results suppressed in the source with nosemgrep are marked as suppressed in the SARIF and are not imported.

docs.title: CodeQL
docs.text:
codeql database create codeql-db --language=python --source-root .
codeql database analyze codeql-db codeql/python-queries \
  --format=sarif-latest --output=codeql.sarif
nephilex import codeql.sarif

In GitHub Actions, github/codeql-action/analyze writes its SARIF to the directory given by its output input (default ../results); pass that file to nephilex import. CodeQL's %SRCROOT% usually names the runner's checkout path. Nephilex reads paths relative to it as relative to --project and prints a warning saying so.

docs.title: gitleaks
docs.text:
gitleaks detect --source . --report-format sarif --report-path gitleaks.sarif
# gitleaks 8.19 and later also accept:
gitleaks dir . --report-format sarif --report-path gitleaks.sarif
nephilex import gitleaks.sarif

gitleaks puts the raw secret in the SARIF snippet. Nephilex masks it before the finding is stored (see Secrets in imported files), but the SARIF file itself still holds the secret: treat it as sensitive, or run gitleaks with --redact.

docs.title: Trivy
docs.text:
trivy fs --format sarif --output trivy.sarif .
nephilex import trivy.sarif

# Container images: paths are inside the image, not the project
trivy image --format sarif --output trivy-image.sarif myapp:1.4.2
nephilex import trivy-image.sarif

Trivy declares its base as file:///; Nephilex treats a base that is the filesystem root as the project root.

docs.title: Bandit
docs.text:
bandit -r . -f sarif -o bandit.sarif
nephilex import bandit.sarif

Recent Bandit releases include the SARIF formatter; older ones need the bandit-sarif-formatter package.

docs.title: Anything else
docs.text: Any tool that writes SARIF 2.1.0 works the same way. Nephilex reads the fields the specification defines and the common extensions listed below; a field it does not understand is ignored.

docs.title: What is preserved
docs.text:
Nephilex finding Taken from scanner sarif:<tool>, from tool.driver.name (sarif:codeql, sarif:semgrep-oss, ...) rule_id <tool>.<ruleId>, for example codeql.py/sql-injection title the rule's shortDescription, else its readable name, else the first line of the message description the result message (text, markdown, or id with arguments) why_vulnerable the rule's fullDescription remediation the rule's help text, with helpUri as a reference (http and https only) location the first physicalLocation: path, start and end line and column snippet the source line(s) from the project file when readable, else region.snippet, then contextRegion.snippet; always redacted cwe properties.tags (external/cwe/cwe-079, CWE-79: ...), properties.cwe, rule.relationships and result.taxa into a CWE taxonomy owasp tags such as OWASP-A03:2021 - Injection tags sarif, the tool name, and the rule's other tags metadata.sarif tool name and version, original rule id, fingerprints and partialFingerprints, logical locations, the source file, and which field set the severity metadata.cve a CVE or GHSA id in the rule id (Trivy)

Rules are looked up by ruleIndex, rule.index with rule.toolComponent (CodeQL keeps its rules in tool.extensions), then by id. A result without a file location keeps its logical location (for example (com.example.Billing.charge)), or the tool name, as a placeholder path.

docs.title: Severity
docs.text:
The first of these that is present and valid wins:

  1. properties["security-severity"] on the result, then on the rule (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep). GitHub's buckets: 9.0 and above is critical, 7.0 high, 4.0 medium, 0.1 low, 0.0 info.
  2. A named severity or issue_severity property (critical, high, medium, low, info; Bandit).
  3. properties["problem.severity"]: error is high, warning medium, recommendation low (CodeQL).
  4. The result level, then the rule's defaultConfiguration.level: error is high, warning medium, note low, none info.
  5. Otherwise medium (SARIF's default level is warning), except for secret findings, which default to high: a committed credential is never "a warning", and gitleaks writes no level at all.

docs.title: Confidence
docs.text: Nephilex has not verified an imported result, so confidence is one step below what the tool claims (precision, confidence or issue_confidence): very-high is high, high medium, medium and low low. A tool that says nothing gets low. Confidence affects the risk score and ordering, not the --fail-on gate.

docs.title: Skipped results
docs.text: Results are not imported when they are not a problem (kind of pass, notApplicable or informational), are baselineState: absent, or carry an accepted suppression (a suppressions entry with status accepted or no status). nephilex import prints how many were skipped and why.

docs.title: Paths and safety
docs.text:
An imported file is untrusted input: it may come from a CI artifact or a pull request. Nephilex therefore:

  • refuses files over 50 MB, JSON nested deeper than 64 levels, NaN or Infinity constants, SARIF versions other than 2.1.0, and more than 100,000 results (a usage error, exit 2);
  • ignores any field of the wrong type instead of trusting it;
  • percent-decodes URIs, accepts / and \ separators and file:// URIs (including file:///C:/...), and resolves uriBaseId through originalUriBaseIds;
  • drops, with a warning, any location that resolves outside the project root: ../ traversal (also percent-encoded), absolute paths elsewhere, other hosts, UNC paths and schemes other than file, http and https;
  • never opens a file outside the root. When it reads a project file to fill a snippet, it resolves symlinks first and skips the file if it leads outside, is not a regular file, is binary or is over the project size limit;
  • strips terminal control sequences from all text.

A uriBaseId that points somewhere else (usually the checkout path on the CI machine) is read as the project root; the relative part is still checked against it.

docs.title: Secrets in imported files
docs.text:
Every snippet and message is run through the same redaction Nephilex's secrets scanner uses before the finding is stored. For a secret finding (from a secret scanner such as gitleaks, a credential CWE, or a rule or tag naming a secret, token, password or key) Nephilex also:

  • masks the exact column span the tool reported, even when the value matches no known pattern;
  • masks the whole snippet when nothing else could be located, as for gitleaks, which stores only the value;
  • removes the masked values from the title, message and help text.

The raw value is never kept in the finding, its metadata or any report.

docs.title: De-duplication
docs.text:
When the same issue is reported twice, the report shows it once. Two findings are the same issue when they come from different scanners, are in the same file, and either

  • both have a line, the lines are at most 2 apart, and they share a CWE; or
  • they name the same advisory (CVE or GHSA id), as Nephilex's dependency scanner and Trivy do for one vulnerable package.

Which finding is kept:

  • with nephilex scan --import-sarif, Nephilex's own finding is kept, because it carries Nephilex's reasoning, remediation and fix support;
  • between two imported findings, the one with the higher severity (then confidence) is kept, the first file given on a tie.

The kept finding lists the others in metadata.also_reported_by and takes the highest severity among them (noted in metadata.severity_raised_by), so importing a file can never make a --fail-on gate pass that the tool on its own would fail. Attack-chain findings are never merged with. Identical results (the same file imported twice, or duplicate results in one file) are collapsed.

docs.title: Baselines, diffs and identity
docs.text:
Each imported finding gets a stable id, sarif:<tool>:<rule>:<hash>. The hash covers the tool, rule and path, plus the result's fingerprints and partialFingerprints when the tool provides them, else the line and snippet.

Baselines, exceptions and the audit log match on a finding's fingerprint. When the tool supplied fingerprints or partialFingerprints (CodeQL, Semgrep and most others do), the fingerprint is rule id, path and the hash from the finding's id (metadata.sarif.fingerprint), which is computed from the tool's fingerprints: the tool designed them to survive edits, and they do not depend on the file being readable. Otherwise it is the same as for Nephilex's own findings: rule id, path and the whitespace-normalized snippet. Because Nephilex reads the snippet from the project file, such a finding keeps its identity when unrelated edits move it, as long as the file is available. Record and compare a baseline the usual way:

nephilex import semgrep.sarif -f json -o baseline.json
# later, in CI: report and gate only on new results
nephilex import semgrep.sarif --baseline baseline.json --fail-on high

--diff origin/main...HEAD keeps only results on changed lines, as for nephilex scan.

docs.title: Using the rest of Nephilex
docs.text:
Imported findings go through the same post-processing as Nephilex's own, in the same order, so every setting below behaves exactly as it does for nephilex scan:

  • Allowlist and exceptions: allow: entries in .nephilex.yml and .nephilex/exceptions.yml apply to imported findings. Match a rule by its original id (rule: py/sql-injection) or the prefixed one.
  • Inline suppressions: nephilex-ignore comments apply on trusted projects, as for a scan.
  • exclude_paths from config also drops imported findings in those paths.
  • Project context: .nephilex/context.yml lowers findings under internal_paths, raises those under data_classification and adjusts likelihood by exposure, recording each change in metadata.context. See Project context.
  • Audit log: an allowlist entry, exception, inline comment or baseline that hides an imported finding is recorded in .nephilex/audit.log on trusted local projects. See Audit log.
  • Attack chains are built from the imported findings as from scanner findings.
  • Policy: write a JSON report and check it: nephilex import *.sarif -f json -o results.json then nephilex policy check --report results.json.
  • Enrichment and fixes: imported findings go through the configured AI provider (offline heuristics by default; --no-ai turns it off) and, with --patches, patch generation. Deterministic fixes are attached with --no-ai too.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: The same as nephilex scan: 0 when the gate passes, 1 when a finding is at or above --fail-on (or fail_on in config), 2 for usage errors, including an unreadable or rejected SARIF file, a missing --project directory and an unknown severity. A result dropped for an unsafe path is a warning, not an error.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only SARIF 2.1.0. Other formats (Semgrep JSON, Trivy JSON) are not read.
  • Only the first location of a result is used. codeFlows, relatedLocations and stacks are not imported, and SARIF fixes are not turned into Nephilex patches.
  • An absolute path outside the project root is dropped, not re-mapped. Use relative paths or originalUriBaseIds (most tools do by default), or run nephilex import from a checkout at the same path the tool used.
  • If the tool gives no fingerprints, the project file is not available and the SARIF has no snippet, the baseline fingerprint falls back to the line number, so such a finding is reported again after it moves.
  • nephilex-ignore: <rule> cannot name rule ids that contain / (CodeQL); use an allow: entry or a rule-less nephilex-ignore instead.
  • Markdown in messages is kept as text, not rendered.

docs.title: Infrastructure scanning
docs.text: Nephilex checks deployment and platform configuration as part of a normal scan, or through focused commands when you only want one area.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Scanners What it checks nephilex cicd . cicd GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkinsfile nephilex container . container, iac Docker Compose, Dockerfiles, Kubernetes manifests nephilex cloud . cloud, iac Terraform and CloudFormation (AWS, Azure, GCP) nephilex infrastructure . cicd, container, cloud, iac All infrastructure checks in one pass nephilex inventory . (analysis only) Export languages, deps, CI/CD, container, IaC file lists nephilex scan . all Includes infrastructure plus SAST, secrets, dependencies, etc.

Common flags (same on each focused command):

nephilex cicd . --fail-on high          # exit 1 for High+ findings (CI gate)
nephilex container . -o report.json     # JSON output
nephilex cloud . --quiet                # suppress progress lines

docs.title: CI/CD scanner (cicd)
docs.text:
Targets workflow files under .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, and Jenkinsfile.

Examples of what it flags:

  • pull_request_target with checkout of untrusted PR code
  • Mutable action references (uses: org/action@main instead of a commit SHA)
  • Over-broad permissions: blocks
  • Untrusted GitHub event fields interpolated into run: scripts
  • Hardcoded secrets in workflow YAML
  • curl | bash in pipeline steps

Example in CI:

- name: CI/CD security
  run: nephilex cicd . --fail-on high --quiet

See also ci-cd.md for the full GitHub Action and SARIF integration.

docs.title: Container scanner (container + iac)
docs.text:
The container scanner focuses on Compose and Dockerfile extras (privileged services, host networking, :latest tags, secret-like environment variables).

The iac scanner covers the same Dockerfiles plus Kubernetes YAML and base Terraform resource rules. nephilex container runs both so you get one command for container posture.

Examples:

  • Compose privileged: true or network_mode: host
  • image: nginx:latest without a digest
  • Dockerfile ENV PASSWORD=... committed in the image layer
  • Kubernetes privileged: true, runAsNonRoot: false, hostNetwork: true

Live cluster assessment (running pods, RBAC, exposed services) is not in the core. Add-on packages can provide it as an extra CLI command through the nephilex.commands entry point (see Writing plugins).

docs.title: Cloud scanner (cloud + iac)
docs.text:
Static analysis of infrastructure-as-code. No cloud API credentials are used; Nephilex reads files in the repository.

Examples:

  • Security groups or firewall rules open to 0.0.0.0/0
  • Public S3 ACLs or disabled public access blocks
  • Unencrypted RDS or storage
  • IAM policies with Action: * on Resource: *
  • Azure allow_blob_public_access = true
  • GCP bucket bindings for allUsers

Live cloud API posture checks (querying AWS, Azure, or GCP accounts) are not part of the core, which only reads files in the repository.

docs.title: Tuning in .nephilex.yml
docs.text:
Focused commands honor project config for excludes and severity floors:

min_severity: low
exclude_paths:
  - vendor/
  - "**/fixtures/**"
scanner_options:
  iac:
    # reserved for future per-scanner knobs

To run only infrastructure scanners in a full scan:

nephilex scan . -s cicd,container,cloud,iac

docs.title: LLM / AI-application security
docs.text:
Codebases now embed LLM calls, agent frameworks, MCP servers and model loading, and that surface has its own vulnerability classes that generic SAST does not cover. Nephilex ships two scanners for it, with every finding mapped to an id in the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 and to a CWE:

Scanner Reads Needs llm Python and JS/TS files that touch an LLM or agent stack (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, Ollama, Google GenAI, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP SDKs for Python and TypeScript, OpenAI Agents, transformers) The data-flow rules need the [ast] extra (pip install "nephilex[ast]"); the line rules always run agent-config MCP and agent configuration files (.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json, .claude/settings.json, Windsurf mcp_config.json, Cline, Roo Code, Gemini CLI); AI-assistant instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules/*.mdc and the rest, listed below); MCP server source in Python and JS/TS Nothing extra; the MCP tool-description rule needs the [ast] extra

Every finding carries owasp and metadata.owasp_llm (for example LLM05:2025-Improper Output Handling) and the tags ai-security plus llm, agent and/or mcp, so the JSON and SARIF output can be filtered or routed by category.

nephilex scan ./my-ai-app --scanners llm,agent-config
